PullRequest.Title: Markdown Editor: don't resync the webview on dirty-state changes
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/342170

With `files.autoSave: afterDelay`, typing in the Markdown Editor could lose keystrokes and make the caret jump: a sentence typed as `it might be better if` was saved as `it mbe better if`.

## Cause

The Markdown Editor webview applies typing locally and sends each change to the extension as an edit tagged with an *edit epoch*. The extension advances the epoch and pushes the document text back into the webview only when the document changes externally. Edits tagged with an older epoch are then ignored.

VS Code also fires `onDidChangeTextDocument` when only the dirty state changes, with empty `contentChanges`: on save, and on the first edit after a save. The provider handled such an event like an external change. It advanced the epoch and sent the document text to the webview. Edits that were still in flight from the webview became stale and were dropped, and the webview's newer text was replaced by the older document text. Every auto save therefore caused up to two such resynchronizations. On large files, where the webview is slow per keystroke, each one lost several characters.

## Fix

Ignore document change events without content changes in the Markdown Editor provider. Real external changes, including save participants that modify text, still resynchronize the webview as before.

## Validation

- New bridge test `keeps accepting edits across saves without resynchronizing the renderer`: it saves between two edits of the same epoch. It fails without the fix (second edit dropped, `update` posted) and passes with it.
- Reproduced in Code OSS on a ~96 KB Markdown file with `files.autoSave: afterDelay` (1000 ms). Before: characters were missing from the saved text. After: the full typed sentence was saved.

The typing lag on large files (problem 2 in the issue) is tracked separately in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344635.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each save-related dirty-state event with no text changes redundantly triggered an O(document size) getText/full-content RPC transfer and renderer replaceSourceText; with after-delay autosave this repeated during active typing and could occur up to twice per save without coalescing.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large Markdown documents incurred repeated full-model replacement during autosave, adding IPC, allocation, and renderer work on the typing path and causing visible typing lag/caret disruption.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added contentChanges.length === 0 guard returns before diagnostics refresh, epoch invalidation, full-document RPC serialization, and renderer model replacement, while content-bearing external changes continue through the existing synchronization path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base event listener at line 645 handled every same-document onDidChangeTextDocument event. For empty dirty-state/save events it fell through to postAuthoritativeUpdate, which reads the entire document (postAuthoritativeUpdate at current lines 435-442), sends the full content over the extension/webview RPC boundary, and the renderer handles update by constructing a StringValue and calling model.replaceSourceText (markdown-editor-src/editor.ts:190-198). The new bridge test demonstrates two saves can occur between same-epoch edits and expects zero renderer updates. Blame identifies the listener's introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing in the Markdown custom editor while after-delay autosave saves the active file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A webview edit is applied to the TextDocument and the filesystem save completes; the resulting empty onDidChangeTextDocument dirty-state event now returns immediately. Before the diff, that event invalidated the edit epoch, copied the full document, sent it over extension/webview RPC, and synchronously replaced the renderer model on the active typing path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filesystem save per autosave trigger; the added test performs two bounded saves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Autosave already wrote the file. The production diff does not change filesystem call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save itself must complete for persistence, but the PR does not add or move this production filesystem operation; it only changes handling of the subsequent empty document-change event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the complete document through markdownEditorRenderer.update to the webview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Now zero calls for each matching empty dirty-state event; before the diff, every such event issued one full-document request with no coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every same-document event, including empty save/dirty-state events, fell through to postAuthoritativeUpdate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the fix, the request reached the active renderer during typing and caused replaceSourceText; the new early return removes it from the autosave path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy and encode the complete Markdown text into the RPC update payload, then construct StringValue in the renderer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Now zero full-document payloads per empty event; previously one payload and renderer replacement per event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Empty events performed O(document length) allocation and renderer model replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from the save-related typing path by the added guard.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost before the fix scaled linearly with Markdown document length and with autosave frequency; an empty save event caused a full-content synchronization rather than O(1) handling. There is one active provider listener per open Markdown editor panel, filtered to its document.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The filesystem save is managed by VS Code. Before the guard, each matching empty change event independently launched postAuthoritativeUpdate without local coalescing or awaiting it in the event callback, so multiple save/dirty-state events could leave RPC replacements in flight. After the diff, effective synchronization concurrency for empty events is zero.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved in document synchronization. Warm versus cold state does not reduce the old cost because every empty event re-read and re-sent the entire current document; the new guard eliminates that work deterministically.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added line directly gates the event, the old fallthrough reaches getText plus renderer.update, the renderer calls replaceSourceText, and the new test asserts no updates across saves.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact milliseconds and event count vary with document size, autosave settings, transport overhead, and renderer complexity. This affects the size of the improvement, not confidence that the removed full-document work existed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes repeated O(document size) synchronization and renderer work from a frequent autosave path; this concrete regression fix was recorded internally.

Scenarios.Scenario: External edits or save participants that actually modify Markdown text
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A same-document event with one or more contentChanges still refreshes diagnostics, compares against expected local content, and sends an authoritative full-document update only when the change is external. The new guard does not run for this case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh diagnostics and, for non-local external changes, send the full authoritative document to the webview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one diagnostics request and one document update per qualifying content-bearing event, unchanged from the base behavior after local-edit echo suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same diagnostics and authoritative update calls ran for content-bearing external changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to synchronize real external content into the visible renderer; it remains on the external-edit propagation path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One listener invocation per TextDocument change event; an authoritative update transfers content proportional to document length. Effective cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: External events retain the existing fire-and-report behavior and have no newly introduced limiter or burst. The diff neither increases request frequency nor changes concurrency for content-bearing events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No content cache serves this path. expectedWebviewContent suppresses the echo for accepted local webview edits; the diff leaves that deduplication unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contentChanges.length greater than zero bypasses the new return and executes the original code unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External edit frequency and document sizes vary, but the PR leaves both boundary cardinality and payload size unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; required external synchronization retains its previous cost and behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced autosave, local typing, external edit, RPC serialization, renderer replacement, and filesystem-save paths. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. The production guard is a concrete repeated-work fix; test-only filesystem operations are bounded and do not affect product performance.
